paper_title: The metamorphosis of semi-classical mechanisms of confinement: from monopoles on R^3 x S^1 to center-vortices on R^2 x T^2 (Guvendik, 2024, JHEP)
core_reasoning_2:
\noindent\textbf{Claim.} For the monopole EFT with potential
\[
V(\sigma_i)=-\zeta_m\left(e^{i\sigma_1}+\cdots+e^{i\sigma_{N-1}}+e^{-i(\sigma_1+\cdots+\sigma_{N-1})}+\text{c.c.}\right),
\]
the constant critical points in the fundamental domain are
\[
\sigma_k^*=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\rho,
\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,N-1,
\]
and, with $\zeta_m=K e^{-S_I/N}$ and four-dimensional theta angle $\theta$, their energy branches are
\[
E_k(\theta)=-2NK e^{-S_I/N}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right).
\]

\noindent\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{(P1)}&\quad N\geq 2,\quad \sigma=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\sigma_j\mu_j,\quad \rho:=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\mu_j.\\
\mathrm{(P2)}&\quad V(\sigma_i)=-\zeta_m\left(e^{i\sigma_1}+\cdots+e^{i\sigma_{N-1}}+e^{-i(\sigma_1+\cdots+\sigma_{N-1})}+\text{c.c.}\right).\\
\mathrm{(P3)}&\quad \frac{\partial V}{\partial \sigma_i}=0\Longleftrightarrow \sigma_i=-(\sigma_1+\cdots+\sigma_{N-1})\pmod{2\pi}\quad \text{for all }i.\\
\mathrm{(P4)}&\quad \alpha_a\cdot \rho\equiv 1\pmod N\quad \text{for }a=1,\ldots,N.\\
\mathrm{(P5)}&\quad E(\sigma;\theta):=-2K e^{-S_I/N}\sum_{a=1}^{N}\cos\left(\alpha_a\cdot \sigma+\frac{\theta}{N}\right).\\
\mathrm{(P6)}&\quad \cos(x+2\pi m)=\cos x\quad \text{for all }m\in\mathbb{Z}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
\sigma_i=-(\sigma_1+\cdots+\sigma_{N-1})\pmod{2\pi}
&\quad \text{for every }i && \text{by (P3)},\\
\sigma_1&=\sigma_2=\cdots=\sigma_{N-1}=:s \pmod{2\pi} && \text{same right-hand side},\\
s&=-(N-1)s \pmod{2\pi} && \text{substitute }\sigma_i=s,\\
Ns&=0\pmod{2\pi} && \text{add }(N-1)s,\\
s&=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\pmod{2\pi},\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,N-1 && \text{solutions modulo }2\pi.
\end{align}
\begin{align}
\sigma^*_k
&=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\sigma_j\mu_j && \text{by (P1)},\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\frac{2\pi k}{N}\mu_j && \text{critical value }\sigma_j=s,\\
&=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\mu_j && \text{factor common scalar},\\
&=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\rho. && \text{by (P1)}
\end{align}
\begin{align}
\alpha_a\cdot \sigma^*_k
&=\alpha_a\cdot \left(\frac{2\pi k}{N}\rho\right) && \text{definition of }\sigma_k^*,\\
&=\frac{2\pi k}{N}(\alpha_a\cdot\rho) && \text{linearity},\\
&\equiv \frac{2\pi k}{N}\pmod{2\pi} && \text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}
\begin{align}
E_k(\theta)
&:=E(\sigma_k^*;\theta) && \text{definition of branch energy},\\
&=-2K e^{-S_I/N}\sum_{a=1}^{N}\cos\left(\alpha_a\cdot \sigma_k^*+\frac{\theta}{N}\right) && \text{by (P5)},\\
&=-2K e^{-S_I/N}\sum_{a=1}^{N}\cos\left(\frac{2\pi k}{N}+\frac{\theta}{N}\right) && \text{previous congruence and (P6)},\\
&=-2NK e^{-S_I/N}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right). && \text{sum of }N\text{ identical terms}
\end{align}

\noindent\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\sigma_k^*=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\rho,\\quad E_k(\theta)=-2NK e^{-S_I/N}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right),\quad k=0,\ldots,N-1}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\noindent\textbf{Claim.} In the magnetic-flux basis $\{|\nu_i\rangle\}_{i=1}^{N}$, the tight-binding Hamiltonian
\[
H=\sum_{i=1}^{N}E_0|\nu_i\rangle\langle \nu_i|-\sum_{i=1}^{N}K e^{-S_m-i\theta/N}|\nu_i\rangle\langle \nu_{i+1}|+\text{h.c.},
\quad |\nu_{N+1}\rangle:=|\nu_1\rangle,
\]
is diagonalized by electric-flux states
\[
|e_k\rangle:=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\omega^{-ki}|\nu_i\rangle,
\qquad \omega:=e^{2\pi i/N},
\]
with matrix eigenvalues
\[
E_k^{\rm QM}(\theta)=E_0-2K e^{-S_m}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right).
\]
Equivalently, after subtracting $E_0$ and using the paper's branch-energy normalization $\varepsilon_k:=N(E_k^{\rm QM}-E_0)$ with $S_m=S_I/N$, one obtains
\[
\varepsilon_k(\theta)=-2N K e^{-S_I/N}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right),
\]
which is the same multi-branch dependence as the monopole EFT branch energy.

\noindent\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{(P1)}&\quad N\geq 2,
\quad \omega:=e^{2\pi i/N},
\quad \omega^N=1.\\
\mathrm{(P2)}&\quad \langle \nu_i|\nu_j\rangle=\delta_{ij},
\quad |\nu_{N+1}\rangle:=|\nu_1\rangle.\\
\mathrm{(P3)}&\quad T:=\sum_{i=1}^{N}|\nu_i\rangle\langle \nu_{i+1}|.\\
\mathrm{(P4)}&\quad H=E_0 I-Ke^{-S_m-i\theta/N}T-Ke^{-S_m+i\theta/N}T^{\dagger}.\\
\mathrm{(P5)}&\quad |e_k\rangle:=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\omega^{-ki}|\nu_i\rangle,
\quad k=0,1,\ldots,N-1.\\
\mathrm{(P6)}&\quad e^{ix}+e^{-ix}=2\cos x.\\
\mathrm{(P7)}&\quad S_m=S_I/N,\quad \varepsilon_k(\theta):=N\left(E_k^{\rm QM}(\theta)-E_0\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
T|\nu_j\rangle
&=\sum_{i=1}^{N}|\nu_i\rangle\langle \nu_{i+1}|\nu_j\rangle && \text{by (P3)},\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{N}|\nu_i\rangle\delta_{i+1,j} && \text{by (P2)},\\
&=|\nu_{j-1}\rangle && \text{cyclic index convention}.
\end{align}
\begin{align}
T|e_k\rangle
&=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\omega^{-kj}T|\nu_j\rangle && \text{by (P5)},\\
&=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\omega^{-kj}|\nu_{j-1}\rangle && \text{previous line},\\
&=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\omega^{-k(\ell+1)}|\nu_{\ell}\rangle && \text{set }\ell=j-1,\\
&=\omega^{-k}|e_k\rangle. && \text{by (P5)}
\end{align}
Since $T^\dagger$ has the conjugate eigenvalue on $|e_k\rangle$,
\begin{align}
T^{\dagger}|e_k\rangle&=\omega^{k}|e_k\rangle && \text{unitarity of the cyclic shift}.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
H|e_k\rangle
&=\left(E_0-Ke^{-S_m-i\theta/N}\omega^{-k}-Ke^{-S_m+i\theta/N}\omega^{k}\right)|e_k\rangle && \text{by (P4)},\\
&=\left(E_0-Ke^{-S_m}e^{-i(\theta+2\pi k)/N}-Ke^{-S_m}e^{i(\theta+2\pi k)/N}\right)|e_k\rangle && \text{by (P1)},\\
&=\left(E_0-2K e^{-S_m}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right)\right)|e_k\rangle && \text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}
Using the branch-energy normalization in (P7),
\begin{align}
\varepsilon_k(\theta)
&=N\left(E_k^{\rm QM}(\theta)-E_0\right) && \text{by (P7)},\\
&=N\left[-2K e^{-S_m}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right)\right] && \text{matrix eigenvalue},\\
&=-2N K e^{-S_I/N}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right). && \text{use }S_m=S_I/N
\end{align}

\noindent\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{H|e_k\rangle=\left(E_0-2K e^{-S_m}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right)\right)|e_k\rangle,
\quad |e_k\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\omega^{-ki}|\nu_i\rangle,
\quad \varepsilon_k(\theta)=-2N K e^{-S_I/N}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\noindent\textbf{Claim.} The deformed two-dimensional $Z_N$ TQFT
\[
S_{2d}=\frac{iN}{2\pi}\int_M \phi\,da-2\zeta_v\int_M d^2x\cos(\phi+\theta/N)
\]
localizes on $N$ branches with energy densities
\[
\varepsilon_k(\theta)=-2\zeta_v\cos\left(\frac{2\pi k+\theta}{N}\right),
\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1.
\]
For $\theta\in(-\pi,\pi]$, the charge-$q$ Wilson loop obeys an area law
\[
\langle W_q(C)\rangle\sim \exp[-(\varepsilon_q(\theta)-\varepsilon_0(\theta))A_D],
\qquad C=\partial D,
\]
so its string tension is $T_q=\varepsilon_q(\theta)-\varepsilon_0(\theta)$.

\noindent\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{(P1)}&\quad \phi\sim \phi+2\pi,
\quad a\text{ is a }U(1)\text{ gauge field},
\quad M\text{ has area }A_M.\\
\mathrm{(P2)}&\quad S_{2d}=\frac{iN}{2\pi}\int_M \phi\,da-2\zeta_v\int_M d^2x\cos(\phi+\theta/N).\\
\mathrm{(P3)}&\quad \int Da\,\exp\left(-\frac{iN}{2\pi}\int_M\phi\,da\right)\text{ imposes }e^{iN\phi}=1.\\
\mathrm{(P4)}&\quad e^{iN\phi}=1\Longleftrightarrow \phi=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\pmod{2\pi},\quad k=0,\ldots,N-1.\\
\mathrm{(P5)}&\quad Z(\theta)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\exp[-\varepsilon_k(\theta)A_M].\\
\mathrm{(P6)}&\quad \text{For }\theta\in(-\pi,\pi],\text{ the }k=0\text{ branch is the vacuum branch.}\\
\mathrm{(P7)}&\quad \text{A charge-}q\text{ Wilson loop on }C=\partial D\text{ places branch }q\text{ inside }D\text{ and branch }0\text{ outside }D.\\
\mathrm{(P8)}&\quad A_D:=\operatorname{area}(D),\quad A_{M\setminus D}=A_M-A_D.
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
e^{iN\phi}=1
&\Longleftrightarrow \phi=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\pmod{2\pi},\quad k=0,\ldots,N-1 && \text{by (P3)--(P4)},\\
S_{2d}\big|_{\phi=2\pi k/N}
&=\frac{iN}{2\pi}\int_M \frac{2\pi k}{N}\,da-2\zeta_v\int_M d^2x\cos\left(\frac{2\pi k}{N}+\frac{\theta}{N}\right) && \text{by (P2)},\\
&=ik\int_M da-2\zeta_v A_M\cos\left(\frac{2\pi k+\theta}{N}\right) && \text{constant }\phi\text{ and area }A_M.
\end{align}
The branch-dependent energy density is therefore
\begin{align}
\varepsilon_k(\theta)
&:=-2\zeta_v\cos\left(\frac{2\pi k+\theta}{N}\right) && \text{read from the area term},\\
Z(\theta)&=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\exp[-\varepsilon_k(\theta)A_M] && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}
For the Wilson loop, the dominant vacuum contribution without insertion is
\begin{align}
Z_0(\theta)&\sim \exp[-\varepsilon_0(\theta)A_M] && \text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}
With the charge-$q$ Wilson loop inserted,
\begin{align}
Z_q(C;\theta)
&\sim \exp[-\varepsilon_q(\theta)A_D]\exp[-\varepsilon_0(\theta)(A_M-A_D)] && \text{by (P7)--(P8)},\\
\langle W_q(C)\rangle
&:=\frac{Z_q(C;\theta)}{Z_0(\theta)} && \text{definition as an insertion ratio},\\
&\sim \frac{\exp[-\varepsilon_q(\theta)A_D]\exp[-\varepsilon_0(\theta)(A_M-A_D)]}{\exp[-\varepsilon_0(\theta)A_M]} && \text{substitute the two partition functions},\\
&=\exp[-(\varepsilon_q(\theta)-\varepsilon_0(\theta))A_D] && \text{cancel the outside-vacuum factor}.
\end{align}
Thus
\begin{align}
T_q&:=\varepsilon_q(\theta)-\varepsilon_0(\theta) && \text{definition of string tension from the area exponent}.
\end{align}

\noindent\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\varepsilon_k(\theta)=-2\zeta_v\cos\left(\frac{2\pi k+\theta}{N}\right),\qquad
\langle W_q(C)\rangle\sim e^{-T_qA_D},\qquad T_q=\varepsilon_q(\theta)-\varepsilon_0(\theta)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\noindent\textbf{Claim.} In the two-stage compactification on $\mathbb{R}^2\times (S^1)_2\times (S^1)_3$ with $n_{23}=1$, the twisted boundary condition
\[
\widetilde{\sigma}_{p}(x_0,x_1,x_2+L_2)=e^{2\pi ip/N}\widetilde{\sigma}_{p}(x_0,x_1,x_2)
\]
forces the mode expansion
\[
\widetilde{\sigma}_{p}(x_0,x_1,x_2)=\sum_{k_2\in\mathbb{Z}}\widetilde{\sigma}_{p,k_2}(x_0,x_1)
\exp\left[\frac{2\pi i}{L_2}\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right)x_2\right],
\]
and gives the two-dimensional mass spectrum
\[
M^2_{p,k_2}=\left(\frac{2\pi}{L_2}\right)^2\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right)^2.
\]
For $p=1,\ldots,N-1$, there is no zero mode; the lightest classical dual-photon mass is $\omega=2\pi/(NL_2)$.

\noindent\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{(P1)}&\quad N\geq 2,
\quad p\in\{1,
\ldots,N-1\},
\quad k_2\in\mathbb{Z},
\quad L_2>0.\\
\mathrm{(P2)}&\quad \widetilde{\sigma}_{p}(x_0,x_1,x_2+L_2)=e^{2\pi ip/N}\widetilde{\sigma}_{p}(x_0,x_1,x_2).\\
\mathrm{(P3)}&\quad \text{A Fourier mode }e^{iqx_2}\text{ has }-\partial_2^2 e^{iqx_2}=q^2e^{iqx_2}.\\
\mathrm{(P4)}&\quad \text{After reduction to }\mathbb{R}^2,\text{ the contribution }q^2\text{ is the mass squared }M^2.\\
\mathrm{(P5)}&\quad \min_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}|k+p/N|=\frac{1}{N}\quad \text{for }p=1\text{ or }p=N-1.
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent\textbf{Derivation.}
Let a single mode have $x_2$ dependence $e^{iqx_2}$. Then
\begin{align}
e^{iq(x_2+L_2)}&=e^{2\pi ip/N}e^{iqx_2} && \text{by (P2)},\\
e^{iqL_2}&=e^{2\pi ip/N} && \text{cancel }e^{iqx_2},\\
qL_2&=2\pi\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right),\quad k_2\in\mathbb{Z} && \text{equality of phases modulo }2\pi,\\
q&=\frac{2\pi}{L_2}\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right). && \text{divide by }L_2
\end{align}
Therefore the full expansion is
\begin{align}
\widetilde{\sigma}_{p}(x_0,x_1,x_2)
&=\sum_{k_2\in\mathbb{Z}}\widetilde{\sigma}_{p,k_2}(x_0,x_1)
\exp\left[\frac{2\pi i}{L_2}\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right)x_2\right] && \text{sum over allowed phases}.
\end{align}
Using (P3)--(P4),
\begin{align}
M^2_{p,k_2}
&=q^2 && \text{by (P3)--(P4)},\\
&=\left(\frac{2\pi}{L_2}\right)^2\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right)^2 && \text{substitute }q.
\end{align}
For $p\in\{1,
\ldots,N-1\}$,
\begin{align}
k_2+\frac{p}{N}&\neq 0 && \text{integer plus non-integer fraction},\\
M^2_{p,k_2}&>0 && \text{by the spectrum above},\\
M_{\rm min}&=\frac{2\pi}{L_2}\min_{p,k_2}\left|k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right| && \text{minimize the positive mass},\\
&=\frac{2\pi}{NL_2} && \text{by (P5)}.
\end{align}

\noindent\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\widetilde{\sigma}_{p}=\sum_{k_2\in\mathbb{Z}}\widetilde{\sigma}_{p,k_2}e^{\frac{2\pi i}{L_2}(k_2+p/N)x_2},\qquad
M^2_{p,k_2}=\left(\frac{2\pi}{L_2}\right)^2\left(k_2+\frac{p}{N}\right)^2,
\qquad M_{\rm min}=\omega=\frac{2\pi}{NL_2}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\noindent\textbf{Claim.} In the $\ell_D\gg L_2\gg L_3$ regime, the monopole-monopole interaction on $\mathbb{R}^2$ becomes short-ranged:
\[
V(x)=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{2\pi}K_0(\omega |x|)
\sim \frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(\frac{NL_2}{|x|}\right)^{1/2}e^{-2\pi |x|/(NL_2)}
\quad (\omega |x|\to\infty),
\]
where $\omega=2\pi/(NL_2)$. Hence the flux tube has characteristic transverse size
\[
r_v=\omega^{-1}=\frac{NL_2}{2\pi}.
\]

\noindent\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{(P1)}&\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^2,
\quad r:=|x|>0,
\quad L_2>0,
\quad \omega:=\frac{2\pi}{NL_2}>0.\\
\mathrm{(P2)}&\quad V(x):=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\int\frac{d^2p}{(2\pi)^2}\frac{e^{ip\cdot x}}{p^2+\omega^2}.\\
\mathrm{(P3)}&\quad \int\frac{d^2p}{(2\pi)^2}\frac{e^{ip\cdot x}}{p^2+\omega^2}=\frac{1}{2\pi}K_0(\omega r).\\
\mathrm{(P4)}&\quad K_0(z)\sim \left(\frac{\pi}{2z}\right)^{1/2}e^{-z}\quad \text{as }z\to\infty.\\
\mathrm{(P5)}&\quad \text{The characteristic range of a Yukawa interaction with mass }\omega\text{ is }\omega^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
V(x)
&=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\int\frac{d^2p}{(2\pi)^2}\frac{e^{ip\cdot x}}{p^2+\omega^2} && \text{by (P2)},\\
&=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{2\pi}K_0(\omega r) && \text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
For $\omega r\to\infty$,
\begin{align}
V(x)&\sim \frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{2\pi}\left(\frac{\pi}{2\omega r}\right)^{1/2}e^{-\omega r} && \text{by (P4)},\\
&=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{2\pi}\left(\frac{\pi}{2(2\pi/(NL_2))r}\right)^{1/2}e^{-(2\pi/(NL_2))r} && \text{by (P1)},\\
&=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{2\pi}\left(\frac{NL_2}{4r}\right)^{1/2}e^{-2\pi r/(NL_2)} && \text{simplify denominator},\\
&=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(\frac{NL_2}{r}\right)^{1/2}e^{-2\pi r/(NL_2)}. && \text{extract }1/2
\end{align}
The exponential factor determines the range:
\begin{align}
r_v&:=\omega^{-1} && \text{by (P5)},\\
&=\left(\frac{2\pi}{NL_2}\right)^{-1} && \text{by (P1)},\\
&=\frac{NL_2}{2\pi}. && \text{invert}
\end{align}

\noindent\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{V(x)=\frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{2\pi}K_0(\omega |x|)
\sim \frac{A_{ij}}{L_2}\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(\frac{NL_2}{|x|}\right)^{1/2}e^{-2\pi |x|/(NL_2)},
\qquad r_v=\frac{NL_2}{2\pi}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_8:
\noindent\textbf{Claim.} In the abelianized long-distance theory, a large fundamental Wilson loop on $\mathbb{R}^2$ detects the fractionalized monopole flux $f=2\pi\nu_i$ as a center vortex:
\[
W(C)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(i\int_D \nu_j\cdot f\right)
=\exp\left(-\frac{2\pi i}{N}\Theta_D(x)\right),
\]
so that
\[
W(C)=e^{-2\pi i/N}\quad \text{if the vortex lies in }D,
\qquad
W(C)=1\quad \text{if the vortex lies outside }D.
\]

\noindent\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{(P1)}&\quad C=\partial D,
\quad \Theta_D(x)=1\text{ if }x\in D,
\quad \Theta_D(x)=0\text{ if }x\notin D.\\
\mathrm{(P2)}&\quad W(C)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(i\int_D \nu_j\cdot f\right).\\
\mathrm{(P3)}&\quad \nu_i\cdot\nu_j=\delta_{ij}-\frac{1}{N}.\\
\mathrm{(P4)}&\quad f=2\pi\nu_i\,\Theta_D(x)\quad \text{for the flux tube piercing }D.\\
\mathrm{(P5)}&\quad e^{2\pi i}=1.
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
\int_D \nu_j\cdot f
&=\int_D \nu_j\cdot\left(2\pi\nu_i\Theta_D(x)\right) && \text{by (P4)},\\
&=2\pi(\nu_j\cdot\nu_i)\Theta_D(x) && \text{constant flux through }D,\\
&=2\pi\left(\delta_{ij}-\frac{1}{N}\right)\Theta_D(x) && \text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
Substituting into the Wilson loop gives
\begin{align}
W(C)
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(2\pi i\left(\delta_{ij}-\frac{1}{N}\right)\Theta_D(x)\right) && \text{by (P2)},\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(2\pi i\delta_{ij}\Theta_D(x)\right)\exp\left(-\frac{2\pi i}{N}\Theta_D(x)\right) && \text{split exponential}.
\end{align}
Because $\Theta_D(x)\in\{0,1\}$,
\begin{align}
\exp\left(2\pi i\delta_{ij}\Theta_D(x)\right)&=1 && \text{by (P1) and (P5)},\\
W(C)
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp\left(-\frac{2\pi i}{N}\Theta_D(x)\right) && \text{substitute previous line},\\
&=\exp\left(-\frac{2\pi i}{N}\Theta_D(x)\right) && \text{sum of }N\text{ identical terms}.
\end{align}
The two possible cases are therefore
\begin{align}
x\in D&\Longrightarrow \Theta_D(x)=1\Longrightarrow W(C)=e^{-2\pi i/N} && \text{by (P1)},\\
x\notin D&\Longrightarrow \Theta_D(x)=0\Longrightarrow W(C)=1 && \text{by (P1)}.
\end{align}

\noindent\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{W(C)=e^{-2\pi i\Theta_D(x)/N}=\begin{cases}e^{-2\pi i/N},&x\in D,\\1,&x\notin D.\end{cases}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
